plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single three-dimensional sketch of two nested surfaces over a labeled coordinate frame, with the x axis coming forward to the lower left, the y axis running right, and the z axis vertical. The outer surface is a downward-opening paraboloid drawn as a translucent shell shaded in blue and salmon; its apex sits on the z axis at the marked point (0, 0, 2), and it widens as it descends, closing in a broad elliptical rim near the xy-plane. Nested inside is a cone with its vertex at the origin, opening upward and shaded darker blue-gray, its circular top rim appearing as an ellipse partway up the paraboloid's interior. Two horizontal arrows carry the equations: the left arrow points to the inner cone and reads z = sqrt(x^2 + y^2), the right arrow points to the outer shell and reads z = 2 - x^2 - y^2. Dashed segments trace the hidden part of the z axis and the far side of the base rim. Nesting one surface inside the other makes the enclosed solid legible, with a curved dome above and a pointed conical floor below. The sketch fixes the region whose volume is to be set up as a triple integral in cylindrical coordinates.

elements: z-axis: vertical arrow up, labeled 'z', with dashed portion where it is hidden inside/behind the surfaces
y-axis: arrow to the right, labeled 'y'
x-axis: arrow forward toward lower-left, labeled 'x'
Downward-opening paraboloid z = 2 - x^2 - y^2, translucent shell shaded blue-to-salmon, apex on the z-axis at (0,0,2), widening downward
Elliptical base rim of the paraboloid where it meets the xy-plane (radius sqrt(2)), far half drawn dashed
Upward-opening cone z = sqrt(x^2 + y^2) with vertex at the origin, darker blue-gray shading
Elliptical top rim of the cone at the intersection circle r = 1, z = 1, drawn partway up inside the paraboloid
Point marker and text label '(0, 0, 2)' at the paraboloid apex
Left horizontal leader arrow pointing at the inner cone with label 'z = sqrt(x^2 + y^2)'
Right horizontal leader arrow pointing at the outer paraboloid shell with label 'z = 2 - x^2 - y^2'
Dashed hidden-line segments: hidden part of z-axis and far side of the base rim
Vertical probe segment at radius r running from the cone surface (z = r) up to the paraboloid surface (z = 2 - r^2) — interactive element
Ground-plane radial marker / dashed radius from origin out to the probe location in the xy-plane

interactions.teaches: The cone sits nested inside the paraboloid dome, and the two surfaces meet along a single horizontal circle — visible only when the solid is turned in depth.
At each radius r the solid is bounded below by the cone z = r and above by the paraboloid z = 2 - r^2; the vertical gap shrinks to zero exactly at r = 1, which is why the r-integration stops there.
interactions.label: Radial coordinate r

interactions.teaches: The same two surfaces have much simpler descriptions in cylindrical coordinates (z = r and z = 2 - r^2), because both depend only on distance from the z-axis.
interactions.label: Equation form

demo_steps.title: The nested surfaces
demo_steps.narration: A downward-opening paraboloid with apex at (0,0,2) encloses an upward-opening cone with vertex at the origin. The solid of interest lies between them.

demo_steps.title: A vertical slice at small r
demo_steps.narration: At radius r = 0.3 the vertical segment runs from the cone at z = 0.3 up to the paraboloid at z = 1.91 — a tall column of the solid.

demo_steps.title: Switch to cylindrical labels
demo_steps.narration: The surfaces become z = r and z = 2 - r^2. Both depend only on r, so every vertical slice at the same radius is identical — the radial symmetry is highlighted.

demo_steps.title: The surfaces meet at r = 1
demo_steps.narration: Setting r = 2 - r^2 gives r = 1, z = 1. The segment closes to a point: this circle is the outer radial limit of the region.

demo_steps.title: Beyond the intersection
demo_steps.narration: Past r = 1 the cone rises above the paraboloid, so no solid remains — confirming the bounds 0 <= r <= 1, r <= z <= 2 - r^2, 0 <= theta <= 2pi.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units = math units. Axes: +Y is screen-right (y-axis, arrow at y = 3), +Z is screen-up (z-axis, arrow at z = 3), +X points forward toward lower-left (x-axis, arrow at x = 3); origin at screen center-bottom of the figure. Paraboloid z = 2 - (x^2+y^2) drawn for 0 <= z <= 2, i.e. r from 0 to sqrt(2) ~ 1.414; apex point at (0,0,2) with text label '(0, 0, 2)' offset up-right of the apex. Cone z = sqrt(x^2+y^2) drawn for 0 <= z <= 1, vertex at origin, top rim a circle of radius 1 at z = 1 (the exact intersection with the paraboloid, r=1, z=1) which appears as an ellipse roughly two-fifths up the paraboloid's height. Base rim of paraboloid: circle radius 1.414 in the z = 0 plane; the far (back) half of this ellipse is dashed, as is the segment of the z-axis from z = 0 up to about z = 2 that passes behind/inside the surfaces. Colors: paraboloid translucent (opacity ~0.45) with a blue-to-salmon gradient, blue #7f9fc4 / #8fb0d0 on the right-rear and salmon #e6a288 / #dd9a84 on the left-front; cone opaque-ish blue-gray #6e7f9e (opacity ~0.85); axes, dashes and text black #1a1a1a; leader arrows black thin lines. Left leader arrow is horizontal, starting near screen-left at z ~ 1.1 and pointing right into the cone's flank, label 'z = sqrt(x^2 + y^2)' at its tail; right leader arrow is horizontal, starting near screen-right at z ~ 0.8 and pointing left into the paraboloid shell, label 'z = 2 - x^2 - y^2' at its tail. Interactive probe: a vertical line segment at radius r placed in the +X/+Y front-facing quadrant (screen-front-right, toward the viewer) from (r, 0, r) on the cone to (r, 0, 2 - r^2) on the paraboloid, drawn in bright orange #e2661f with small end dots, plus a dashed radius from the origin out to (r,0,0) in the xy-plane with an 'r' tick label. In Cylindrical mode the labels change to 'z = r' (cone) and 'z = 2 - r^2' (paraboloid) and a faint family of concentric circles / a sweeping theta wedge on both surfaces highlights radial symmetry.
interactionPlan.notes: Build both surfaces as ParametricGeometry in (r, theta): cone P(r,th) = (r cos th, r sin th, r) for r in [0,1]; paraboloid P(r,th) = (r cos th, r sin th, 2 - r^2) for r in [0,1.414], ~64 theta segments, 32 radial segments. Use MeshPhongMaterial with side: THREE.DoubleSide, transparent: true, opacity 0.45 for the paraboloid and 0.85 for the cone; apply the blue/salmon gradient via per-vertex colors keyed to the azimuth angle (vertexColors: true) rather than a texture. Render surface rims as separate THREE.Line loops; dashed hidden lines via LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances(). Axes as thin cylinders or Line plus ConeGeometry arrowheads. All text labels ('x','y','z','(0,0,2)', the two equations) as CSS2DObject/HTML overlays so they stay screen-facing and legible while orbiting; equation label text swaps on the toggle with a short cross-fade. The probe segment is a Line whose two endpoints recompute from the slider each frame; clamp/grey it out and show 'surfaces have crossed' styling when r > 1. Keep depthWrite false on the translucent paraboloid so the cone inside remains visible. Default camera: standard isometric pose, OrbitControls with damping, target at (0,0,1).

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for radial coordinate r: the learner increases r from the z-axis outward, the vertical segment between z=r and z=2-r^2 updates until the surfaces meet, showing why cylindrical bounds run from the cone to the paraboloid.
- Toggle between Cartesian equations and cylindrical forms: the learner switches labels from z=sqrt(x^2+y^2) and z=2-x^2-y^2 to z=r and z=2-r^2, and the radial symmetry highlights, clarifying why cylindrical coordinates simplify the setup.

authoredContext:
Let E be the region bounded below by the cone z=x2+y2 and above by the paraboloid z=2−x2−y2. (the figure). Set up a triple integral in cylindrical coordinates to find the volume of the region, using the following orders of integration:

Setting up a triple integral in cylindrical coordinates over a conical region.

A paraboloid with equation z = 2 minus x squared minus y squared opening down, and within it, a cone with equation z = the square root of (x squared + y squared) pointing down.

discrepancies: Color scheme is noticeably muted: the source shows a strong blue↔salmon gradient across the paraboloid shell and a bluish translucent cone, whereas the generated surfaces read as grey/tan with only weak salmon on the left flank.

The interior cone renders very dark and nearly opaque, losing the source's semi-transparent look where the cone is seen through the paraboloid wall; the intersection rim ellipse is also less visually distinct than in the source.

Added elements not in the source (orange probe segment, 'Δz = 1.25' box, 'r = 0.50' dashed radius) sit in the middle of the figure and slightly clutter the default view compared with the clean textbook drawing.

Axis orientation differs slightly: in the source the y-axis runs nearly horizontally to the right and x drops steeply to the lower-left, while the generated view has a more symmetric 30°/30° splay with y angled downward.
Paraboloid base ellipse in the source has a clearly shaded elliptical bottom disc rim with salmon tinting; generated base rim is a thin line with little tonal contrast.
evaluation.notes: Correct surfaces (paraboloid z=2−r² over cone z=r meeting at r=1, z=1), correct axes/labels, and a rich set of genuinely pedagogical interactions (radius probe, Cartesian/cylindrical toggle, guided tour); main weaknesses are washed-out colors versus the source's blue–salmon gradient, an overly dark opaque cone, and probe annotations cluttering the default view.
action_items: Strengthen the vertex-color gradient (deeper #6f93c0 blue to #e8987c salmon) and reduce the cone's opacity/darkness so it reads as a translucent inner surface like the source.
Make the default state cleaner: hide (or fade) the orange probe segment, Δz box and r-label until the slider or tour is first used, so the initial render matches the textbook figure.
Emphasize the intersection circle (r=1, z=1) and the base ellipse (r=√2, z=0) with slightly thicker/darker tube-style lines, as these outlines are prominent in the source.
Adjust axis screen angles so the y-axis is closer to horizontal-right and x drops more steeply to the lower-left, matching the source's projection.

feedback.rationale: Concept, geometry, and interaction structure are correct; the remaining issues are purely rendering details (color gradient, cone opacity, default-state clutter, line emphasis, camera angle) that the generator can fix.

Left leader arrow is horizontal, starting near screen-left at z ~ 1.1 and pointing right into the cone's flank, label 'z = sqrt(x^2 + y^2)' at its tail; right leader arrow is horizontal, starting near screen-right at z ~ 0.8 and pointing left into the paraboloid shell, label 'z = 2 - x^2 - y^2' at its tail. Interactive probe: a vertical line segment at radius r placed in the +X/+Y front-facing quadrant (screen-front-right, toward the viewer) from (r, 0, r) on the cone to (r, 0, 2 - r^2) on the paraboloid, drawn in bright orange #e2661f with small end dots, plus a dashed radius from the origin out to (r,0,0) in the xy-plane with an 'r' tick label. In Cylindrical mode the labels change to 'z = r' (cone) and 'z = 2 - r^2' (paraboloid) and a faint family of concentric circles / a sweeping theta wedge on both surfaces highlights radial symmetry.
interactionPlan.notes: Build both surfaces as ParametricGeometry in (r, theta): cone P(r,th) = (r cos th, r sin th, r) for r in [0,1]; paraboloid P(r,th) = (r cos th, r sin th, 2 - r^2) for r in [0,1.414], ~64 theta segments, 32 radial segments. Use MeshPhongMaterial with side: THREE.DoubleSide, transparent: true, opacity 0.45 for the paraboloid and 0.85 for the cone; apply the blue/salmon gradient via per-vertex colors keyed to the azimuth angle (vertexColors: true) rather than a texture. Render surface rims as separate THREE.Line loops; dashed hidden lines via LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances(). Axes as thin cylinders or Line plus ConeGeometry arrowheads. All text labels ('x','y','z','(0,0,2)', the two equations) as CSS2DObject/HTML overlays so they stay screen-facing and legible while orbiting; equation label text swaps on the toggle with a short cross-fade. The probe segment is a Line whose two endpoints recompute from the slider each frame; clamp/grey it out and show 'surfaces have crossed' styling when r > 1. Keep depthWrite false on the translucent paraboloid so the cone inside remains visible. Default camera: standard isometric pose, OrbitControls with damping, target at (0,0,1).

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure is a single three-dimensional sketch of two nested surfaces over a labeled coordinate frame, with the x axis coming forward to the lower left, the y axis running right, and the z axis vertical. The outer surface is a downward-opening paraboloid drawn as a translucent shell shaded in blue and salmon; its apex sits on the z axis at the marked point (0, 0, 2), and it widens as it descends, closing in a broad elliptical rim near the xy-plane. Nested inside is a cone with its vertex at the origin, opening upward and shaded darker blue-gray, its circular top rim appearing as an ellipse partway up the paraboloid's interior. Two horizontal arrows carry the equations: the left arrow points to the inner cone and reads z = sqrt(x^2 + y^2), the right arrow points to the outer shell and reads z = 2 - x^2 - y^2. Dashed segments trace the hidden part of the z axis and the far side of the base rim. Nesting one surface inside the other makes the enclosed solid legible, with a curved dome above and a pointed conical floor below. The sketch fixes the region whose volume is to be set up as a triple integral in cylindrical coordinates.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for radial coordinate r: the learner increases r from the z-axis outward, the vertical segment between z=r and z=2-r^2 updates until the surfaces meet, showing why cylindrical bounds run from the cone to the paraboloid.
- Toggle between Cartesian equations and cylindrical forms: the learner switches labels from z=sqrt(x^2+y^2) and z=2-x^2-y^2 to z=r and z=2-r^2, and the radial symmetry highlights, clarifying why cylindrical coordinates simplify the setup.

evaluation.notes: Composition, camera, surfaces (paraboloid to z=0 at r=√2, cone to r=1, intersection circle at r=1,z=1), axes and all source labels are faithfully reproduced with excellent pedagogically meaningful interactions (r-slice probe, Cartesian/cylindrical toggle, 5-step guided tour); main weaknesses are washed-out colours versus the source's saturated blue/salmon gradient, a faint inner cone, and a duplicated-looking rim near z = 1.

feedback.rationale: Concept, structure, and interactions are correct; remaining issues are purely rendering details (washed-out colors, faint cone, duplicated rim line, arrowhead) that call for implementation-level styling fixes.

interactions.teaches: The cone sits nested inside the paraboloid dome, and the two surfaces meet along a single horizontal circle — visible only when the solid is turned in depth.
At each radius r the solid is bounded below by the cone z = r and above by the paraboloid z = 2 - r^2; the vertical gap shrinks to zero exactly at r = 1, which is why the r-integration stops there.

interactions.teaches: The same two surfaces have much simpler descriptions in cylindrical coordinates (z = r and z = 2 - r^2), because both depend only on distance from the z-axis.

demo_steps.title: The nested surfaces
demo_steps.narration: A downward-opening paraboloid with apex at (0,0,2) encloses an upward-opening cone with vertex at the origin. The solid of interest lies between them.

demo_steps.title: A vertical slice at small r
demo_steps.narration: At radius r = 0.3 the vertical segment runs from the cone at z = 0.3 up to the paraboloid at z = 1.91 — a tall column of the solid.

demo_steps.title: Switch to cylindrical labels
demo_steps.narration: The surfaces become z = r and z = 2 - r^2. Both depend only on r, so every vertical slice at the same radius is identical — the radial symmetry is highlighted.

demo_steps.title: The surfaces meet at r = 1
demo_steps.narration: Setting r = 2 - r^2 gives r = 1, z = 1. The segment closes to a point: this circle is the outer radial limit of the region.

demo_steps.title: Beyond the intersection
demo_steps.narration: Past r = 1 the cone rises above the paraboloid, so no solid remains — confirming the bounds 0 <= r <= 1, r <= z <= 2 - r^2, 0 <= theta <= 2pi.
